abstract: BACKGROUND: Cervical choriocarcinoma is an extremely rare malignancy that is often misdiagnosed due to its nonspecific symptoms, such as vaginal bleeding. CASE REPORT: A 39-year-old female presented to the emergency department of the First Affiliated Hospital of Sun Yat-sen University with vaginal bleeding and a serum β-human chorionic gonadotropin (β-HCG) level of 229,386 mIU/mL. Initially, she was misdiagnosed with cervical pregnancy and subsequently underwent selective uterine artery embolization and cervical mass excision. However, pathological examination revealed the diagnosis of cervical choriocarcinoma. CONCLUSION: This case highlights the propensity for misdiagnosis of cervical choriocarcinoma. Selective uterine artery embolization proves to be an efficient measure to manage hemorrhage and potentially avoid unnecessary hysterectomy.
abstract_ja: 背景：子宮頸部絨毛癌は膣出血などの非特異的症状のためしばしば誤診される極めて稀な悪性腫瘍です。症例報告：39歳の女性が膣出血および血清β-ヒト絨毛性ゴナドトロピン（β-hCG）レベル229,386 mIU/mLを伴って中山大学第1附属病院の救急科に提示されました。初期は子宮頸部妊娠と誤診され、その後選択的子宮動脈塞栓および子宮頸部腫瘓切除を受けました。しかし、病理学的検査は子宮頸部絨毛癌の診断を明らかにしました。結論：本症例は子宮頸部絨毛癌の誤診の傾向を強調しています。選択的子宮動脈塞栓は出血を管理し、潜在的に不必要な子宮全摘除を回避するための効率的な手段であることが証明されています。
